fields: IAM's name
per-CpG levels and reads
In the field's terms
Per-CpG methylated and total read counts, by cell type
Definition
The atlas's raw counts: methylated reads and total reads at each CpG, for each of the 58 cell types, with 65535 used as the code for blank (no data).
What it does
Enters the chain as atlas pieces feeding the instrument that serves as the ruler for what healthy methylation looks like at every CpG across the 58 cell types.
Why the instrument needs it
The instrument needs these measured counts to build, for each cell type and CpG, the level, the person-to-person spread, and the 95% range used both to identify cells and as the healthy ruler.
How it is obtained or computed

Formula: meth and reads per CpG and type (65535 = blank). Built from published sorted-cell WGBS of healthy donors (Loyfer et al. 2023 and other sources); for each type and CpG the methylated and total read counts give the level, the person-to-person spread and the 95% range, computed from the donors' spread with Student's t interval, not a model fit. Data are split by donor halves so every reading can be tested out of sample.
Where it is read
Per CpG, across 28.2 million CpGs, in whole-genome bisulfite sequencing data for 58 cell types.
Where IAM's Law enters
Not part of IAM's Law: this is a measured input the law uses (law_part: 'not the law itself: a measured input the law uses'), registered at M4, with lf_section 'not part of IAM's Law'.
Long-form section
not part of IAM's Law
Healthy value and how it is set

Default/typical form is set per cell type or fixed, from a cited measurement (source_kind): the counts themselves, as measured in healthy donors, are what define each cell type's own healthy level and its 95% range.

fields: IAM's name
person-to-person spread (donor_sd)
In the field's terms
Person-to-person (inter-individual) variation in methylation level at a CpG site (donor_sd)
Definition
How much healthy people differ at each site: donor_sd per site, with one-library cell types borrowing their lineage's value.
What it does
It enters per site and feeds the Atlas's computation of the healthy range at that CpG for each of the 58 cell types.
Why the instrument needs it

The Atlas is built to be the ruler of what healthy methylation looks like at every CpG, and doing that requires knowing not just the average level but how much healthy donors naturally vary at each site.
How it is obtained or computed

Given as donor_sd per site; for one-library cell types it is borrowed from their lineage's value rather than measured directly. It is derived from published sorted-cell WGBS of healthy donors (Loyfer et al. 2023 and other sources), using methylated and total read counts per type and CpG, and combined with the level via a Student's t interval to form the 95 % range (not a model fit).
Where it is read
Per CpG site, across the 28.2 million CpGs covered by the Atlas, for each of the 58 cell types.
Where IAM's Law enters

Not part of IAM's Law itself: register M4 and the row's own law_part both mark it as 'not the law itself: a measured input the law uses,' and its lf_section is 'not part of IAM's Law.' It is a measured quantity (status: measured, per the atlas) describing donor-to-donor spread, not a term in the Law's equation.
Long-form section
not part of IAM's Law
Healthy value and how it is set

Set per cell type (or, for one-library types, borrowed from their lineage) from measured donor WGBS data; source_kind is 'set per cell type or fixed, from a cited measurement,' with basis 'measured.' No single typical numeric value is given in the records — open: not in the records yet.
Where its value comes from
set per cell type or fixed, from a cited measurement
Its setting on IAM's Law Sphere
not yet on the card
Lever range (what moves, by how much)
open: not written yet
Limits and what is open
For one-library cell types, donor_sd is not independently measured but borrowed from the lineage, so its real person-to-person spread for that specific type is open: not in the records yet.

fields: IAM's name
Identification-only columns (megakaryocytes; provisional)
In the field's terms
Identification-only reference columns for megakaryocyte methylation (provisional)
Definition

A set of columns added so that megakaryocyte DNA, known to be present in bone marrow, plasma, and CSF, is named as itself instead of having its share scattered over four or five other columns (lung interstitial macrophages, erythrocyte progenitors, MEP, eosinophils). It may only say which cell is there.
What it does

It lets the Deconvolver's second deconvolution (--dev-provisional) assign a sample's megakaryocyte fraction to its own named column for identification, rather than letting that fraction be misattributed across other cell-type columns.
Why the instrument needs it

Because megakaryocyte DNA is known to be present in bone marrow, plasma, and CSF, and without a dedicated column its share would otherwise scatter over several unrelated cell types, confusing identification.
How it is obtained or computed

megakaryocytes_v1/v2 (Runtime Matrices/Provisional_References), the 58th column of the IAM Sequencing Atlas v1.1. Sources: GSE87197 single cells (v1, v2), BLUEPRINT bulk (two donors); a recorded test, a recorded test. Basis: measured (identity only). Used in the Deconvolver's second deconvolution (--dev-provisional).
Where it is read
not genome-located
Where IAM's Law enters

law_part states this is 'not the law: instrument (identification)', and lf_section states it is 'not part of IAM's Law'. It is an identification quantity used by the instrument's deconvolution step, not a step in IAM's Law.
Long-form section
not part of IAM's Law
Healthy value and how it is set

This is explicitly never a healthy reference: no instrument reads a sample against it, no band is set from it, and its share is left out of every expected-healthy mix. Its value is set per cell type from a cited measurement (source_kind: 'set per cell type or fixed, from a cited measurement'), drawn from GSE87197 single cells (v1, v2) and BLUEPRINT bulk (two donors).
Where its value comes from
set per cell type or fixed, from a cited measurement
Its setting on IAM's Law Sphere
not yet on the card

open: not written yet
Limits and what is open

It may only say which cell is there; NEVER a healthy reference: no instrument reads a sample against it, no band is set from it, and its share is left out of every expected-healthy mix. Provisional. Not yet on the card.

Atlas pieces: every per-CpG quantity (the sequencing atlas's accessories)
In the field's terms
Per-CpG atlas accessory statistics: read counts, methylation level, cross-donor spread, disorder, donor count, and donor/read half-splits across 28,217,448 CpGs in 58 cell types
Definition
113 parquet pieces covering 28,217,448 CpGs, each carrying per cell type: reads, meth, level, spread, disorder, donors, halfA, halfB, readA, readB.
What it does

It supplies the per-CpG reference quantities that other readings are built from; the chain's array_sites columns are built from them, though the halves and read halves are used by the noise maps and not yet by the in-mix readings.
Why the instrument needs it

The instrument needs these accessories because they are the ruler itself: what healthy is, at every CpG, for 58 cell types, built from methylated and total read counts, the level, the person-to-person spread, and donor-half splits so every reading can be tested out of sample.
How it is obtained or computed

Built from published sorted-cell WGBS of healthy donors (Loyfer et al. 2023 and other sources): for each type and CpG, methylated and total read counts, the level, the person-to-person spread and the 95% range (from the donors' spread with Student's t interval; not a model fit), split by donor halves. On 2026-11-20 the half levels were rebuilt from the.beta inputs without checking against the prior accessories; they agree exactly (corr 1.0000), the only addition being per-half read counts.
Where it is read
Every CpG across 113 parquet pieces, 28,217,448 CpGs total, in the Zenodo IAM Sequencing Atlas v1.2 (pieces57_set*_of_12.tar; bucket seq_atlas/pieces57/).

Sequencing ruler
In the field's terms
Reference provenance check: which healthy reference atlas each sequencing analysis used
Definition

Which ruler each sequencing instrument used. Healthy: the IAM Sequencing Atlas (test: deconvolver and in_mix_levels on the IAM Sequencing Atlas; metaa_sites chosen on IAM-Atlas v2.1, one instrument, one set of sites; state OK).
What it does

It records which reference each downstream instrument drew on: the test_value shows the deconvolver and in_mix_levels both using the IAM Sequencing Atlas, while metaa_sites was chosen on IAM-Atlas v2.1, one instrument, one set of sites.
Why the instrument needs it
The chain needs a shared, named ruler so every instrument's readings are measured against the same healthy reference; this row is not the law itself but a measured input the law uses.
How it is obtained or computed

Obtained by the chain checking which atlas each component used, recorded at test_path sequencing_ruler; the test_value lists deconvolver: IAM Sequencing Atlas, in_mix_levels: IAM Sequencing Atlas, metaa_sites: chosen on IAM-Atlas v2.1 (one instrument, one set of sites), with test_state OK. outputs.name: Sequencing ruler

fields: How it works

From the published sorted-cell libraries (GSE186458), pooled methylated calls and reads per CpG per cell type over 28,217,448 hg19 CpGs: each type's level, person-to-person spread, 95 % range, disorder, donors, and the sealed donor halves (halfA, halfB) and read halves (readA, readB); runtime pieces per use (Deconvolver markers, identity sites, islands, Law Sphere units).
Why

Most methylation atlases are built to deconvolve; this one is also the healthy ruler: purified cells used as controls, so no instrument needs healthy samples from the same run, and the sealed halves let every atlas library be read against healthy it did not build.
Physics
Not a step of IAM's Law: measured healthy reference.
Where the data comes from
GSE186458 (Loyfer et al. 2023, Nature 613:355) sorted-cell WGBS libraries, aligned and counted by the chain's own pipeline.
The numbers
58 columns (57 healthy types plus megakaryocytes as identification only); 113 parquet pieces; 28,217,448 CpGs; type ranges with Student's t quantiles (stage_seq_atlas.range_of_average v3).
Method and standard
Student's t interval from the donors' spread (Student 1908); sealed donor and read halves; two noise maps; null tests on the sphere.
Known-answer test
Healthy passes 3 to 8 read the atlas's own libraries against the other half; never-used libraries as out-of-sample checks.
Limits
(1) One laboratory. (2) 1-3 donors per type per half (the thin ruler). (3) Megakaryocytes are identification only.
Where the result goes
every atlas-referenced instrument; the Zenodo record.
Code
stage_seq_atlas (range_of_average, deconv_reference_of); jobs that build pieces
How to rebuild it
Align GSE186458, count calls and reads per CpG per type and donor, split donors and reads into halves, compute levels, spreads and ranges.
History
Dated entries in the development log (METHYLPHYS_DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md) and the instrument's development record.
records.name: The IAM Sequencing Atlas: the healthy ruler at every CpG
questions: Where does the atlas come from?
Published sorted-cell libraries (GSE186458), aligned and counted by the chain; published on Zenodo with its own DOI.
How many healthy donors actually back the numbers for each cell type?
One to three donors per cell type in each half of the atlas, from one laboratory. That is a real but small sample, stated as a limit of the reference.
instrument record: the rule's limits (one laboratory; 1-3 donors per type per half)
How is the 95% healthy range worked out - is it a statistical model?
No, it is not a model fit. It's calculated directly from the spread across the actual donors using a Student's t interval.
instrument record: field_how description of how the atlas was built
For a cell type with just one sequencing library, how trustworthy is its person-to-person spread estimate?

Not very, for that specific type on its own: when only one library exists, the person-to-person spread isn't independently measured but is borrowed from related cell types in the same lineage. The true person-to-person spread for that individual type is not yet in the records.
instrument record: input describing person-to-person spread (donor_sd) and its limits
Can the megakaryocyte columns be used to judge whether a sample's megakaryocyte DNA is at a healthy level?

No. Those columns exist only so megakaryocyte DNA can be named as itself instead of being wrongly spread across other cell types. No instrument reads a sample against it, no healthy band is set from it, and its share is left out of every expected-healthy mix - it is identification-only and still provisional.
